news.titleTr: Bakanlıktan peynir düzenlemesi: Üretimde ve piyasaya arzında yeni kurallar belirlendi
news.summaryTr: Peynir üretimine yönelik düzenlemeyle süt proteini dışındaki proteinlerin kullanımı yasaklandı. Yeni kurallar kapsamında, çiğ veya hafif ısıl işlem uygulanmış sütten üretilen ve telemesi haşlanmamış peynirlerin piyasaya arz edilmesi için en az 4 ay olgunlaştırılması gerekecek.
news.articleText: Bakanlıktan peynir düzenlemesi: Üretimde ve piyasaya arzında yeni kurallar belirlendi - Peynir üretimine yönelik düzenlemeyle süt proteini dışındaki proteinlerin kullanımı yasaklandı. Yeni kurallar kapsamında, çiğ veya hafif ısıl işlem uygulanmış sütten üretilen ve telemesi haşlanmamış peynirlerin piyasaya arz edilmesi için en az 4 ay olgunlaştırılması gerekecek. - Düzenlemeye göre peynirler, muhafaza, taşıma ve piyasaya arz süreçlerinin tamamında 10 derecenin altındaki sıcaklıklarda tutulacak. Peynir üretiminde süt proteini dışındaki proteinler, nişasta ve nişasta bazlı ürünler, jelatin, soya ürünleri ile süt yağı dışındaki hayvansal ve bitkisel yağların kullanılması yasaklandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığınca hazırlanan, "Türk Gıda Kodeksi Peynir Tebliği", Resmi Gazete'de yayımlanarak yürürlüğe girerken 2015 tarihli tebliğ yürürlükten kaldırıldı. Yeni düzenlemeyle peynirlerin üretim, işleme, muhafaza, taşıma ve piyasaya arzına ilişkin kurallar yeniden belirlendi. Tebliğ kapsamında peynir üretiminde süt proteini dışındaki proteinler, nişasta ve nişasta bazlı ürünler, jelatin, soya ürünleri ile süt yağı dışındaki hayvansal ve bitkisel yağların kullanılması yasaklandı. Yalnızca çeşnili taze peynirlerde, stabilizör amacıyla teknolojinin izin verdiği miktarda nişasta kullanılabilecek. Çiğ sütten veya termizasyon (çiğ sütün işlenmeden veya pastörizasyondan önce raf ömrünü uzatmak ve içindeki mikroorganizma (bakteri) sayısını azaltmak amacıyla uygulanan hafif bir ısıl işlem) uygulanmış sütten üretilen, telemesi haşlanmamış peynirlerin, en az 4 ay olgunlaştırılmadan piyasaya arz edilmesine izin verilmeyecek. Olgunlaştırılmadan satışa sunulacak peynirlerde ise çiğ sütün en az pastörizasyon normlarında ısıl işlemden geçirilmesi gerekecek. Etiketlere 3 milimetre şartı getirildi Düzenlemeyle, peynir etiketlerine ilişkin kurallar da değişti. Ürünlerin yağlılık sınıfı ve olgunlaşma durumu, etiketlerde ürün adıyla birlikte belirtilecek. Olgunlaştırılarak piyasaya arz edilen peynirlerde üretim tarihi de gün, ay ve yıl şeklinde yer alacak. Ayrıca olgunlaştırma süresinin, etikette belirtilmesi zorunlu olacak. Etiketlerde "köy peyniri", "geleneksel peynir", "doğal peynir" ve "çiftlik peyniri" gibi nitelemeler kullanılamayacak. Farklı hayvan türlerinden elde edilen sütlerin karıştırılmasıyla üretilen peynirlerde ise kullanılan süt türleri, miktarlarına göre çoktan aza doğru sıralanarak belirtilecek. Çeşnili peynirlerde toplam çeşni oranı yüzde 6'yı, çeşnili taze peynirlerde ise yüzde 15'i geçemeyecek. Şeker kullanılan çeşnili taze peynirlerin etiketinde, ilave şeker oranına da yer verilecek. En az 120 gün süreyle olgunlaştırılarak üretilen kaşar peynirlerinde, "eski" ibaresi kullanılabilecek. Prosesinde pastörizasyona eşdeğer ısıl işlem bulunmayan çiğ sütten veya termizasyon uygulanan sütlerden üretilen telemesi haşlanmamış peynirlerin etiketlerinde, ürün adı ile aynı yüzde ve en az 3 milimetre punto büyüklüğünde "çiğ sütten üretilmiştir" ibaresi bulundurulacak. Tebliğ kapsamında yer alan ürünlerin etiketinde, peynirin piyasaya sunulduğu biçimine, üretim tekniğine, şekline ve kullanım amacına göre "sürülebilir", "ultrafiltrasyon", "üçgen", "tost, pizza yapımında kullanılabilir" gibi ibareler, tek başına ürün adı olarak kullanılmaması, ürün adı algısı oluşturulmaması ve ürün adının yazıldığı puntodan daha büyük puntoyla yazılmaması kaydıyla kullanılabilecek. İşletmelere uyum için 30 Nisan 2027'ye kadar süre verildi Peynirlerin muhafazası, taşınması ve piyasaya arzı sırasında 10 derecenin altındaki sıcaklıklarda tutulması zorunlu hale getirildi. Eritme peynirinin dökme olarak piyasaya arz edilmesi ve telemenin doğrudan tüketiciye sunulması da yasaklandı. Mevcut gıda işletmecilerine yeni hükümlere uyum sağlamaları için 30 Nisan 2027'ye kadar süre tanındı. Bu tarihten önce piyasaya arz edilen peynirler, raf ömrü sonuna kadar satışta kalabilecek. Ancak yeni düzenlemeye uygun olmayan dilimlenebilir eritme peynirleri, 30 Nisan 2027'den sonra piyasada bulundurulamayacak.

Prosesinde pastörizasyona eşdeğer ısıl işlem bulunmayan çiğ sütten veya termizasyon uygulanan sütlerden üretilen telemesi haşlanmamış peynirlerin etiketlerinde, ürün adı ile aynı yüzde ve en az 3 milimetre punto büyüklüğünde "çiğ sütten üretilmiştir" ibaresi bulundurulacak. Tebliğ kapsamında yer alan ürünlerin etiketinde, peynirin piyasaya sunulduğu biçimine, üretim tekniğine, şekline ve kullanım amacına göre "sürülebilir", "ultrafiltrasyon", "üçgen", "tost, pizza yapımında kullanılabilir" gibi ibareler, tek başına ürün adı olarak kullanılmaması, ürün adı algısı oluşturulmaması ve ürün adının yazıldığı puntodan daha büyük puntoyla yazılmaması kaydıyla kullanılabilecek. İşletmelere uyum için 30 Nisan 2027'ye kadar süre verildi Peynirlerin muhafazası, taşınması ve piyasaya arzı sırasında 10 derecenin altındaki sıcaklıklarda tutulması zorunlu hale getirildi. Eritme peynirinin dökme olarak piyasaya arz edilmesi ve telemenin doğrudan tüketiciye sunulması da yasaklandı. Mevcut gıda işletmecilerine yeni hükümlere uyum sağlamaları için 30 Nisan 2027'ye kadar süre tanındı. Bu tarihten önce piyasaya arz edilen peynirler, raf ömrü sonuna kadar satışta kalabilecek. Ancak yeni düzenlemeye uygun olmayan dilimlenebilir eritme peynirleri, 30 Nisan 2027'den sonra piyasada bulundurulamayacak.

news.summary: Securitize agreed to buy River One to bring stablecoin funding to asset-backed lending and expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.

news.titleTr: Securitize agrees to buy River One to expand into asset-backed lending
news.summaryTr: Securitize agreed to buy River One to bring stablecoin funding to asset-backed lending and expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.
news.articleText: Securitize agrees to buy River One to expand into asset-backed lending Securitize agreed to buy River One to bring stablecoin funding to asset-backed lending and expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. BlackRock-backed tokenization platform Securitize agreed to buy River One, a New York financing firm, in a deal that would expand the tokenization company into asset-backed lending, the company said Monday. The deal would add a new financing layer to Securitize’s platform, expanding into asset-backed lending, according to a Monday release. River One is developing technology that would let lenders tap stablecoin funding. Lenders could use pools of small business loans or receivables as collateral to borrow money and fund new loans. The acquisition would give Securitize a role in arranging credit alongside its existing business issuing and servicing tokenized assets for firms such as BlackRock. The acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. Securitize ranks as the second-largest real-world asset (RWA) platform with $3.7 billion in total RWA value. Ondo ranks first with $4.1 billion, according to RWA.xyz. Securitize announced the deal alongside Q3 results. Revenue rose 13% from a year earlier to $18.6 million, while the company posted a $66.3 million net loss. Securitize said about $60 million of the loss reflected largely noncash expenses and accounting charges tied mainly to its business combination and public listing. Cointelegraph reached out to Securitize and River One for comment. Related: Securitize falls 16% after earnings miss, tokenization revenue drops

news.titleTr: Bitcoin için korkutan senaryo: Ünlü ekonomist yatırımcıları uyardı
news.summaryTr: Ekonomist Peter Schiff, küresel piyasalardaki toparlanmaya rağmen Bitcoin'in zayıf performans göstermesine dikkat çekerek sert düşüş uyarısında bulundu. Kritik destek seviyesinin kaybedildiğini belirten Schiff, yatırımcılara satış çağrısı yaptı.
news.articleText: Bitcoin için korkutan senaryo: Ünlü ekonomist yatırımcıları uyardı Ekonomist Peter Schiff, küresel piyasalardaki toparlanmaya rağmen Bitcoin'in zayıf performans göstermesine dikkat çekerek sert düşüş uyarısında bulundu. Kritik destek seviyesinin kaybedildiğini belirten Schiff, yatırımcılara satış çağrısı yaptı. ABD borsaları, teknoloji hisseleri, altın ve gümüş fiyatlarında toparlanma yaşanırken Bitcoin'in zayıf performans göstermesi, kripto para piyasasına yönelik endişeleri artırdı. Bitcoin, ABD ara seçimlerinin ardından kaydettiği yükselişin önemli bölümünü geri vererek 74-75 bin dolar aralığına geriledi. Bitcoin'e yönelik olumsuz görüşleriyle tanınan Peter Schiff, diğer yatırım araçlarındaki toparlanmaya rağmen kripto para biriminin güç kazanamamasını önemli bir uyarı işareti olarak değerlendirdi. Schiff, Bitcoin'in kritik destek seviyesini kaybettiğini belirterek yatırımcıların daha büyük kayıplarla karşılaşmadan satış yapmaları gerektiğini savundu. Ekonomist, 5 Kasım'da yaptığı açıklamada da Bitcoin'in bir balon olduğunu ileri sürerek yatırımcılara satış çağrısında bulunmuştu. Ancak Schiff'in geçmişte Bitcoin'in kalıcı çöküşüne ilişkin bazı tahminlerinin gerçekleşmediği biliniyor. Bitcoin ETF'lerinden 1,28 milyar dolarlık çıkış Bitcoin fiyatındaki düşüşe paralel olarak spot Bitcoin borsa yatırım fonlarında (ETF) da sermaye çıkışları hızlandı. Geçen hafta Bitcoin ETF'lerinden toplam 1,28 milyar dolarlık net çıkış gerçekleşirken bu rakam haziran sonundan bu yana en yüksek haftalık çıkış olarak kaydedildi. Son haftalardaki satışlarla birlikte Bitcoin ETF'lerinden yıl başından bu yana gerçekleşen kümülatif net çıkış yaklaşık 919 milyon dolara ulaştı. Ekim ayında ise fonlardan 515 milyon dolarlık net çıkış yaşanmıştı. Piyasalardaki satış baskısında Binance'in 6,3 milyar dolarlık siber saldırıya maruz kaldığına ilişkin gelişmeler, ABD ara seçimleri sonrasındaki belirsizlikler ve teknoloji hisselerindeki değer kayıpları etkili olan unsurlar arasında gösterildi.

news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Sayıştay'dan istihdam açıklaması! Alınacak personeller için şartlar neler?
news.summaryTr: Sayıştay Başkanlığı, 3'ü çözümleyici, 13'ü programcı olmak üzere 16 sözleşmeli personel istihdam edecek.
news.articleText: Sayıştay'dan istihdam açıklaması! Alınacak personeller için şartlar neler? - Sayıştay Başkanlığı, 3'ü çözümleyici, 13'ü programcı olmak üzere 16 sözleşmeli personel istihdam edecek. - Kurumun Resmi Gazete'de yer alan ilanına göre, başvurular 11-25 Kasım tarihlerinde e-Devlet üzerinden alınacak. Sayıştay Başkanlığı'ından istihdam açıklaması geldi. Açıklamaya göre 3'ü çözümleyici, 13'ü programcı olmak üzere 16 sözleşmeli personel istihdam edecek. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kurumun Resmi Gazete'de yer alan ilanına göre, başvurular 11-25 Kasım tarihlerinde e-Devlet üzerinden "Sayıştay Başkanlığı-Kariyer Kapısı Kamu İşe Alım" veya Kariyer Kapısı (https://kariyerkapisi.gov.tr) internet sitesinden elektronik ortamda alınacak. Başvuruların değerlendirilmesinin ardından KPSS puan sıralamasına göre her pozisyon için alınacak personel sayısının 10 katı aday, sözlü sınava çağrılacak. Mesleki bilgi ve uygulamayı ölçmeye yönelik sözlü sınavda 70'in üzerinde puan alan adaylar başarılı sayılacak. Başarılı adaylar arasından pozisyon sayısı kadar asil ve aynı sayıda yedek aday belirlenecek. Sınava katılmaya hak kazananların listesi, sınav tarihi ve yeri Sayıştay Başkanlığının internet sitesinden duyurulacak.

news.title: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga skulls to India
news.summary: The remains will be taken to Nagaland, where tribal leaders plan a joint memorial and burial.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga skulls to India
news.summaryTr: The remains will be taken to Nagaland, where tribal leaders plan a joint memorial and burial.
news.articleText: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga skulls to India - Published The University of Oxford has returned the remains of 39 people taken from the Naga community during British colonial rule in India. A delegation of around 30 people from Nagaland, a mountainous state in north-eastern India, attended a ceremony at Oxford's Pitt Rivers Museum on Monday to mark the handover. The remains, most of which are skulls, will be taken back to India and given what Naga tribal leaders have described as a "respectful rest". There are plans to bury them under a joint memorial in a park in Nagaland. Museum director Laura Van Broekhoven described it as "a historic moment that will be part of stories told to next generations". She said the remains were finally on their way home after overcoming "so much red tape everywhere". The human remains were displayed at the Oxford museum for decades before being removed from public view in 2020 as part of what it described as a "decolonisation process". The Pitt Rivers Museum holds more than 6,000 objects associated with Naga culture, believed to be the largest such collection in the world. Most were acquired during British colonial rule in India and Myanmar (the former Burma). The museum's website lists 219 items as human remains. These were added to the museum's collection between 1910 and 1940 and mostly collected by two colonial administrators who were anthropologists. The museum's website, external mentions that the objects collected during this period were "frequently confiscated during punitive military expeditions, rather than freely given". During their visit to Oxford, the Naga delegation also met descendants of one of the anthropologists involved in collecting the remains. "The manner in which these human remains were taken away from our land leaves much for us to speculate," one of the tribal leaders, Thejao Vihienuo, told AFP. "I suspect that nobody would have given the skull of his father or his grandfather as a gift to another person." Anthropologists say that the Naga people once practised head hunting, severing the heads of enemies as trophies. But they also kept the heads of their own chiefs at the centre of villages. The Pitt Rivers Museum, founded in the 19th Century, has previously returned human remains to indigenous communities in Australia, New Zealand and the US. The latest handover to India concerns only the 39 ancestral remains and comes after a visit by a Naga delegation to Oxford in 2025, when it formally requested their return. The museum had announced in September that the remains would be returned to India.

news.title: Independent bookshop closing after rise in bills
news.summary: The Chicken and Frog in Brentwood says business rates and electricity bills have risen dramatically.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Independent bookshop closing after rise in bills
news.summaryTr: The Chicken and Frog in Brentwood says business rates and electricity bills have risen dramatically.
news.articleText: Independent bookshop closing after rise in bills - Published An independent bookshop described as being a "haven" for families and neurodivergent children has announced it will close after 14 years. The Chicken and Frog says it will leave Brentwood town centre in January after a huge increase in its bills and business rates. Owner Natasha Radford, aka "Mrs Chicken", also says the town's footfall has been so low that at times she has gone a whole day without a sale. The 53-year-old said she had been busy since announcing the news, with customers coming in for a hug and a farewell. "It means the world because running your own business is difficult. It becomes all-consuming," said Radford, a former teacher. "So, to know that we've had a positive impact on people's lives... it's huge." The shop's absence will leave behind more than just empty bookshelves, as it runs workshops and provides a sensory space. Stephanie took her neurodivergent child to the shop and said the news was "truly heartbreaking" and that it would be an "immense loss" to Brentwood. The 36-year-old teacher described it as an "incredible haven" of "knowledge, support and community". "Natasha and her husband treated everyone who came into their shop as a close friend and went above and beyond to help," she said. "Her love for children and their wellbeing was felt in every part of that shop and every club and session she ran." - Budget 2026: Key points at a glance - Published28 October Radford said her profit margins were thin, and a book she typically bought in at £4.05 would then sell for £6.99. The business did not get the "deep discounts that the big boys get", she explained. On top of that, she said her electricity bills had tripled since first opening, and that what she paid annually in business rates had increased from £2,868 in 2024 to £8,435 this year. The amount many businesses are paying in rates has increased because the government reduced its temporary 75% "relief" discount, external to 40% in April 2025. Rates are also dictated by market rental value, and Radford pointed out that this disproportionately affected a town close to London like Brentwood. Radford said communities felt "fragmented" and allowing hubs to close was a "massive oversight" by the government. An HM Treasury spokesperson told the BBC that the autumn Budget gave High Street businesses "more breathing space". Traders will now only pay business rates once their rateable value reaches £18,000 - up from £12,000. However, the spokesperson accepted that some areas were "more expensive than others", meaning certain shops would not benefit. Rental value was a "commercial decision" between landlords and businesses, they added. Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below. "Her love for children and their wellbeing was felt in every part of that shop and every club and session she ran." - Budget 2026: Key points at a glance - Published28 October Radford said her profit margins were thin, and a book she typically bought in at £4.05 would then sell for £6.99. news.title: Holiday hunger bill to face final Stormont hurdle
news.summary: The new law would would help poorer families with food costs during school holidays.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Holiday hunger bill to face final Stormont hurdle
news.summaryTr: The new law would would help poorer families with food costs during school holidays.
news.articleText: Holiday hunger bill to face final Stormont hurdle - Published A proposed law which would help poorer families with food costs during school holidays is to face its final hurdle in the Northern Ireland Assembly later on Tuesday. Some parents and charities have welcomed the Holiday Meal Payments Bill, external, which was brought forward by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker. It would create a new payment for families whose children receive free school meals, which would be made outside of term time to help with the cost of food. But Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) Education Minister Paul Givan has been consistently critical of the legislation, warning it will immediately cost his budget £20m a year at a time when all departments are struggling financially. Why was the bill introduced? Baker said he was motivated to introduce it by some of his experiences of breakfast clubs and meal schemes in youth work. "There was a young boy, about the same age of my youngest, around seven years old," he explained. "He was filling his wee pockets up and we caught on to this. "To cut a long story short, he was bringing home food for his siblings because there just wasn't enough food in the house." Baker said all ministers had choices to make and the legislation alone could not solve child poverty, but would act as an "early intervention". Children are eligible for free school meals if their family's household income is below £15,390 a year. Northern Ireland is the only UK region without government-funded holiday food support, after the Department of Education (DE) ended its £27-per-fortnight holiday meal grant in 2023. Baker's legislation was introduced in the Northern Ireland Assembly in March and has been scrutinised by members of the legislative assembly (MLAs) on a number of occasions over the past nine months. What have campaigners and charities said? Community and voluntary groups have been publicly supportive of the bill, with some staging a demonstration at Stormont on Monday in a bid to urge MLAs to get it over the finish line. Louise McCullough, a mum-of-three from east Belfast, was among those who spoke at the event. She said her children receive free school meals and that she would be directly affected by the legislation. "There are so many working families who need this, it will change their lives and be massively impactful," she told BBC News NI. "I can't afford to work full time because of the cost of childcare, and the cost of living. "We have to do what we can and schemes like free school meals make a difference but so much more needs done... if you can't find money for hungry children what are you doing? "Our government should be scaffolding our families properly." Edel Diamond from the South West Belfast Foodbank said organisations like hers had been "filling in the gaps" to help struggling families. "We shouldn't have to - it's incumbent on our executive to put these initiatives forward," she said. "This will make such a difference to families we're seeing daily." What is the education minister's view? Paul Givan has previously warned that his department does not have funding for the scheme, so MLAs would be voting to cut education spending if they support it. Last month, his department tabled amendments that would have given him power to delay its implementation, but these were rejected by a majority of parties. On Monday, Democratic Unionist Party leader Gavin Robinson accused Sinn Féin of "reckless irresponsibility" over the proposed legislation. He branded the bill an "absurdity" when Stormont's finances were "already overstretched", but Sinn Féin argued it would give families "much-needed support". Robinson added: "This minister is already having to cut his cloth in a way that's going to be difficult and damaging for families." Ulster Unionist leader Jon Burrows said his party would not support the bill, saying that it was "undermining" the executive's case for asking London for additional funding to solve its budget impasse. Although the DUP and UUP are set to vote against the bill on Tuesday, Sinn Féin is expected to have enough support from Alliance and SDLP MLAs to ensure the bill passes. - Published30 March 2023 - Published12 October

news.title: New chief outlines main issues facing Isle of Man
news.summary: The chief minister says connectivity and food storage were among his top government priorities.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: New chief outlines main issues facing Isle of Man
news.summaryTr: The chief minister says connectivity and food storage were among his top government priorities.
news.articleText: New chief outlines main issues facing Isle of Man - Published The chief minister of the Isle of Man has said reliance on imports, risks of transport disruption, and pressure on household finances are among the main challenges facing the new government. The warning came after recent storms disrupted sea and air connections, and questions over how prepared the island is for more prolonged supply problems. Chris Thomas outlined plans to strengthen food security and connectivity, but said emergency preparedness was not among his top five priorities. The chief minister, ard-shirveishagh in Manx, said: "It is a serious issue. We need to improve connectivity through the airport and through Douglas Harbour." He said ensuring "the firms that bring our supplies to us... can get to the island will be a big focus for this government". He acknowledged that more needed to be done around emergency planning and public information, adding the government had held workshops on the issue in 2025 and would look to improve communication with residents. Food security One area of focus was reducing the island's reliance on imported food through greater support for local agriculture, Thomas said. He said one of his first meetings in the role was with the Manx National Farmers' Union, with discussions focusing on maximising local production and reducing supply risks. He also highlighted the need to improve storage and warehouse capacity. Thomas said there was "substantial building going on" on Cooil Road in Braddan, to "optimise the amount of storage we have". But the island's ability to maintain supplies remained closely linked to the reliability of its transport connections, he said. He said: "We had the worst possible situation at the end of October where we had some runway lights out on our airport and we had storms at the harbour." Improvements were needed at the airport, including air traffic control services, to help provide more reliable and affordable routes, he added. The ard-shirveishagh said sea connectivity was another priority, with the government facing ongoing questions about the Steam Packet's vessels and the suitability of the new vessel for Douglas Harbour. He confirmed that the purchase of another vessel remains on pause until harbour issues, including the need for dredging, have been addressed. Cost of living Thomas said putting more money back into people's pockets would be central to the government's approach, pointing to the increase in personal tax allowances introduced in the February budget. He argued that creating a "smaller, smarter, more efficient, more effective" government would help reduce pressure on taxpayers while allowing people to retain more of their income. He also acknowledged the impact of international events on fuel and food prices, and said the government needed to focus on tackling the underlying problems affecting people's lives. While he encouraged residents to take sensible steps to manage their own risks, he said household stockpiling was not something he wanted to make a major government priority. news.title: Poundland crisis 'could see all businesses suffer'
news.summary: Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Poundland crisis 'could see all businesses suffer'
news.summaryTr: Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators.
news.articleText: Poundland crisis 'could see all businesses suffer' - Published A potential collapse of Poundland could impact all businesses on the high street, a West Midlands business owner has said. Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from creditors until Thursday. Dr Lewis Haydon runs Raybloc, a radiation-shielding specialist firm in Willenhall. He told the BBC that it has been a challenging time for businesses over the past few years, especially since retailer Wilko collapsed in 2023. "It's a real shame because we need these people to be going to the high street. [It] is all about income - income for the people [and] income for the businesses on the high street. If that income, the cash flow, isn't there, all businesses suffer." Haydon added: "As an entrepreneur around that area, it's a real shame. Because we've grown up understanding the success stories about Poundland - how it started off as a market stall and it gets larger and larger to a national success. "It gives us a lot of uncertainty that this may happen to us as a business as well. "All the employees that we employ, they're all thinking: 'Could this happen to us as well?'" He added it was "not good news" this close to Christmas. Speaking to BBC Radio WM on Friday, Haydon said the move could also put pressure on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), who he said would struggle to hire those affected by the collapse. "If there's another 12,000 people looking for work in the community, it puts pressure on us, the small and medium-sized enterprises, to employ more people." Poundland founder, Steve Smith, said two or three thousand suppliers, particularly those that work exclusively with Poundland, would also be caught up in any collapse. A second buyer, London-based Xyra Group, has made a rescue bid for the discount retailer as it teeters on the brink of collapse. US-based owner Gordon Brothers has already rejected a rival bid from an Irish property group which would have saved its 12,000 staff. Gordon Brothers said the business has faced years of instability and "remains challenged and vulnerable". Sources familiar with Xyra's offer said the firm is proposing to immediately pay off £12.5 million of an outstanding £30 million loan on Poundland's books. Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, committed at the meeting to prioritising offers that protect its stores and workforce. 'We need to stop decline of the high street' Raj Kandola, from The Black Country Chamber of Commerce, said the impact on people's livelihood "doesn't bear thinking about" and called on the government to help find a solution. "It comes down to the government creating a platform which helps businesses flourish, looking at how we can reform business rates even further to stop this decline of the high street." While the uncertainty lingers, Kandola said there is still hope for the region. "Businesses across the Black Country remain very resilient. In the last 10 years they have seen the fallout from Brexit, Covid-19, the energy price hike following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and the majority of them still continue to display remarkable amount of resilience and continue to move forward." "There are obviously very wide ranging concerns but we shouldn't lose sight of the fact that the Black Country remains open for business." news.title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
news.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

news.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, cybersecurity firm CertiK urged exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that North Korean hackers used newly created memecoins to launder stolen funds and European regulators sought industry participants to help establish common standards for tokenized securities. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain. EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities The European Central Bank, European Commission and European Securities and Markets Authority are seeking nominations for an industry-led group that will draft common standards for holding and settling tokenized securities. Eligible applicants include EU industry associations, global institutions, private firms and fintech companies. They can apply to the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG) by Nov. 27, with work set to begin in January 2027, according to a release published Monday. The three EU institutions will participate as observers. The group will develop technical and market standards to help companies hold and settle tokenized securities across different distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms and ensure those platforms can work with existing financial systems. The group aims to produce an initial set of standards by early 2028, according to its mandate. The standards will support Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative to develop a blueprint for Europe’s tokenized financial markets. The institutions warned that fragmentation could limit the benefits of tokenization and said the group may recommend ways for EU authorities to encourage firms to adopt its standards. In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a system that allows financial institutions to settle wholesale transactions in tokenized assets in central bank money.

news.title: Polish unity on show as thousands join silent march for Krakow shooting victims
news.summary: Fiercely proud of its reputation for safety, Poland has been profoundly shaken by Saturday's attack, writes Sarah Rainsford.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Polish unity on show as thousands join silent march for Krakow shooting victims
news.summaryTr: Fiercely proud of its reputation for safety, Poland has been profoundly shaken by Saturday's attack, writes Sarah Rainsford.
news.articleText: Polish unity on show as thousands join silent march for Krakow shooting victims - Published Thousands of people joined a silent march through central Krakow on Monday night, in memory of those killed and injured when a gunman went on a violent rampage at the weekend. The crowd were led by Poland's president and prime minister, the bitter political rivals putting on a rare show of unity after the country's deadliest attack in modern times. As they reached the historic Market Square, a bugler played from the tower. Many people were carrying flowers or candles to leave at the shrines that now dot the cobblestones, each one marking a spot where someone died. Fiercely proud of its reputation for safety, Poland has been profoundly shaken by this attack. It has left people struggling to make some kind of sense of what happened. Both were members of the Swit Starachowice sports club, where there is a shooting range. A spokesman recalls Michal Oksinski as unremarkable: average competition results and normal behaviour. He had been just three times this year, most recently in August with his father. The club spokesman is adamant that it does not train combat firing, only shooting from a fixed point. Gun ownership in Poland has grown considerably since war broke out in Ukraine just across the border, but this is the first mass shooting anyone here can remember. Inevitably, it has brought scrutiny of the checks over who qualifies to handle such weapons, including psychological tests, as Michal Oksinski passed all of them. On Monday, the government announced an urgent review. At the spot where Oksinski's car was intercepted and he was shot by police there is another memorial, this one in honour of the officers still in hospital. Some have brought flowers, but a girl called Bianka has left a card that reads: "Thank you Mr Policemen, get better soon." A couple of steps away, there's a series of bullet holes in the glass. "This man was a real hero, he didn't hesitate," Ania says, referring to officer Jakub Kulik who was shot in the chest. His condition remains serious. "We're here to help him fight for his life." "Nothing like this has never happened before, it's terrible," a young man called Wojtek tells me. He's only glad that the gunman responsible for such horror turned out to be Polish. "People here are already against immigration, so that would have been even worse." Ania thinks Poles will pull through, though the country's image as a low-crime oasis has been shattered. Most of all, she's angry that Michal Oksinski died without being held to account for the devastation. "I think we deserve to know why." - Published2 days ago - Published21 hours ago - Published1 day ago

news.title: HIVE, MARA mine more Bitcoin but earn less as crypto prices fall

news.titleTr: HIVE, MARA mine more Bitcoin but earn less as crypto prices fall
news.summaryTr: Both miners reported higher Bitcoin production but lower mining revenue and rising electricity costs as they expanded their AI infrastructure businesses.
news.articleText: HIVE, MARA mine more Bitcoin but earn less as crypto prices fall Both miners reported higher Bitcoin production but lower mining revenue and rising electricity costs as they expanded their AI infrastructure businesses. Update (Nov. 10, 2026, 7:31 am UTC): This article has been updated to include details of MARA’s $1.1 billion Bitcoin sale and its repayment of $750 million in Bitcoin-backed loans. HIVE Digital Technologies and MARA Holdings mined more Bitcoin in the September quarter than a year earlier but reported lower mining revenue, as weaker Bitcoin prices outweighed gains in production. According to their latest regulatory filings, HIVE’s Bitcoin production increased 49% to 1,070 Bitcoin (BTC), while mining revenue fell 7.4% to $76 million. MARA reported a similar pattern, with production rising 5% to 2,247 BTC and Bitcoin mining revenue dropping 34% to $159 million. MARA also disclosed that it sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion after the quarter ended Sept. 30. It used $750 million of the proceeds to repay its Bitcoin-backed term loans in full, releasing 17,477 BTC it had pledged as collateral. Both companies reported higher power bills and equipment charges. HIVE’s electricity costs rose 20% to $45.6 million, while MARA’s purchased energy costs increased 12% to $48.1 million as it expanded its owned mining operations. HIVE also recorded a $31.2 million noncash write-down on mining equipment, citing “depressed mining economics,” while MARA separately wrote off $12 million involving mining rigs and equipment under restructuring plans. Both results add to signs of pressure on Bitcoin mining economics. American Bitcoin last week reported weaker mining margins despite a treasury-driven quarterly profit, while Core Scientific said it plans to leave mining entirely by year-end. HIVE and MARA expand AI businesses alongside mining Unlike Core Scientific, HIVE and MARA are both continuing to invest in Bitcoin mining alongside artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. HIVE’s HPC hosting revenue rose 71% to $8.8 million in the September quarter, accounting for 10.4% of total revenue. The company has described its strategy as combining cash flow from mining with recurring revenue from AI infrastructure. Related: American Bitcoin’s $126M profit masks mining pressure as rivals turn to AI HIVE said it anticipates spending up to $493 million over 36 months to expand its HPC operations, including acquiring land, building out data center infrastructure and buying up GPUs. The company reported spending $145.3 million toward that expansion as of the filing. HIVE also plans to spend about $35 million converting its Toronto facility into a Tier-III data center. Meanwhile, it continues to expand its mining infrastructure, targeting a 100-megawatt substation expansion at its Yguazú site in Paraguay during 2026. MARA is also developing AI infrastructure through its Exaion subsidiary and a partnership with Starwood Digital Ventures. It said it intends to operate sites that can shift between workloads depending on economics, demand and grid conditions, with Bitcoin mining remaining the foundation of its platform. Treasury gains lift MARA profit, HIVE reports quarterly loss HIVE’s Nasdaq-listed shares fell 1.7% to $1.78 in after-hours trading Monday, according to Google Finance, after closing the regular session up 1.7% at $1.81. The company reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $84.9 million, down 2.7% from a year earlier but above the $79.4 million consensus estimate listed by MarketBeat. Meanwhile, MARA reported net income attributable to common stockholders of $634.4 million, up from $123.1 million a year earlier, and included substantial fair-value gains on digital assets and digital asset receivables. MARA reported quarterly revenue of $164.2 million, down 35% year-on-year, and diluted earnings of $1.28 a share, up from 27 cents, while its shares were little changed at $6.64 in after-hours trading Monday after closing up 4.6%. Magazine: Should you leave Australia to avoid paying 47% tax on crypto gains?

news.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

items.summary: Huang, who is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, is far more important to the future of the world order than other tech bosses.

items.titleTr: Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security
items.summaryTr: Huang, who is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, is far more important to the future of the world order than other tech bosses.
items.articleText: Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security - Published Jensen Huang has the air of the late Steve Jobs about him. I have interviewed both, and the up-close charisma - and occasionally scratchy genius - is shared. Both sported a signature item of black clothing, although Huang opts for a leather jacket rather than the Apple founder's turtle neck. Both are innovators revered in the tech world. However, Huang is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Everything you have heard about Artificial Intelligence (AI) over the past few months - good, bad, revolutionary and catastrophic - is dependent on having the most powerful frontier AI models. In turn they depend on the most powerful microchips, and for years that has been this very company, Nvidia, led by Huang, and his technology rooted in repurposed games graphics and the manufacturing prowess of Taiwan. Names such as Gracehopper, Vera and Rubin mean almost nothing to the public, but are the names of chips powering the creation of AI models transforming the world. I met Huang as he held court with reporters and offered words of encouragement for the UK's tech future during US President Donald Trump's state visit to the UK in September last year. It was also right in the middle of his attempts to get Trump to lift export bans to China of some of the highest performing AI chips, specifically the H200. An export ban on a less powerful chip had already been lifted. He was, I suggested to him, one of the few people who could walk into the White House to meet Trump, and a few days later meet President Xi Jinping in Beijing. He made no secret of his views, nor his assessment that he had persuaded Trump of his case. "President Trump is very clear. He wants America to win and and President Xi wants China to win, and it's possible for both of them too. And the reason for that is because it's not a zero-sum game. The advance of human society is not a zero-sum game." He is probably the only person in the world that could have spoken that sentence with the authority that he might have heard personally from both these superpower leaders. Differing views on security risks However, his view about "zero-sum game" is not backed by many in national security circles. Their view is that the race to the most advanced forms of AI is entirely zero sum, and requires the West - and the US in particular - to take critical action to hold back Chinese advancement. The country that creates the most powerful AI systems, from the most powerful chips, will win, in terms of scientific development, of cracking encryption, economic growth and cyber-weapons. He made a further argument: Far from being a national security challenge, it was, in fact, better for the US that the world "including China" became dependent on US systems, what they called the "American tech stack", with Nvidia chips at its core. Huang then went even further than that, saying that President Trump "is very clear-eyed" about the idea that "this computing technology is not a national security concern". He told me "any military is smart enough to build their military on top of their own indigenous technology, and not rely on an adversary to build their technology, build their military capability". What does this show us? At that time, which is the same moment now being independently investigated over national security concerns and alleged Chinese espionage, Huang was making clear public arguments to lift export bans, and seemed to have a clear idea of President Trump's views. More than that, he was also disputing the idea that his technology, in China's hands, was any type of national security concern. Nvidia is the absolute epicentre of the AI tech boom in the US and of the global race for AI supremacy. Even if the boom turned to bust, Nvidia is still expected to remain in rude health. It has actual hard revenues of about $400bn this year. Monday's drop of about 4% of its value reflects new and extraordinary risks at this junction of tech and global politics, but the chipmaker is still worth more than $4 trillion. - Published1 hour ago - Published13 hours ago - Published9 hours ago

items.titleTr: Kim Kardashian's Skims offers refunds for $148 advent calendar after backlash
items.summaryTr: The contents of the calendar, including hair clips and keychains, have been widely criticised on social media.
items.articleText: Kim Kardashian's Skims offers refunds for $148 advent calendar after backlash - Published Kim Kardashian's Skims is offering customers refunds for its $148 (£110) advent calendar which has been widely criticised on social media. The accessories advent calendar promised "twelve days of fun surprises" but has been mocked online for the quality of its contents, such as hair clips and keychains, with some comparing them to something you would find down the back of a sofa. A spokesperson for Skims has told a number of media outlets "for some, the calendar didn't meet expectations" and the company has "personally contacted every customer" to offer a full refund or credit to put towards other products". The BBC has contacted Skims for comment. The shapewear and clothing business was co-founder by Kardashian in 2019 and has made the reality TV star a billionaire, according to Forbes magazine. Skims was valued at $5bn in 2025 when it raised millions of dollars in new funding.

items.titleTr: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
items.summaryTr: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow have all sent delegations to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
items.articleText: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say - Published Trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have begun in Abu Dhabi. Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said yesterday that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. "An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X. Ahead of the meeting, the two US envoys met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials in Abu Dhabi, and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was adamant that France, the UK and Germany "will indeed be in the meeting room". European officials are wary of Russia trying to secure a deal with the US on future "collective security" without them, and Moscow and Kyiv's positions on ending the conflict are still far apart. A key area of disagreement between the two involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is by now mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk which it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those sections, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged that the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it's attacked again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans. The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022. The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since. Since then, European leaders - who have been largely excluded from peace talks – have pushed to be involved in the process amid concerns that decisions about the security of their continent would be made without them. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged on Monday to include Nato allies and EU members into any "meaningful discussions about Europe's security architecture". President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly stated Kyiv wanted Europe to be part of the talks. The US official said the Americans would propose moving into a multilateral format bringing the Europeans into the discussion. "Hopefully we'll get the Russians on board," the official said, while acknowledging that "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans." Since the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success. Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union. After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine which "might involve all of Europe". Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result into a fair peace. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believes Trump wants "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Putin start real negotiations is by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi will include Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv is sending several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations." "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." items.articleText: Bir günlük grevin Avrupa ekonomilerine maliyeti: Almanya ilk sırada - Euronews'ün Eurostat verileri üzerinden yaptığı hesaplamaya göre, çalışanların yüzde 20'sinin bir gün iş bırakması Almanya'da 2,5 milyar, Fransa'da 1,6 milyar ve İtalya'da 1,2 milyar euroluk üretim kaybına yol açabilir. Sık tekrarlanan grevler ise ekonomik maliyeti artırıyor. Avrupa'da grevlerin ekonomilere maliyeti ülkelerin ekonomik büyüklüğüne ve iş bırakma eylemlerinin sıklığına göre değişiyor. Euronews'ün Eurostat'ın 2025 yılı gayrisafi yurt içi hasıla (GSYH) verileri üzerinden yaptığı hesaplamaya göre, çalışanların yüzde 20'sinin bir gün iş bırakması halinde Almanya ekonomisinde yaklaşık 2,5 milyar euroluk üretim kaybı yaşanabilir. Almanya'yı 1,6 milyar euroyla Fransa, 1,2 milyar euroyla İtalya izliyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İspanya'da 2012'den bu yana iki büyük sendikanın birlikte düzenlediği ilk genel grev öncesinde yayımlanan analizde, Avrupa ülkelerinin grevlerden kaynaklanabilecek ekonomik kayıpları karşılaştırıldı. Hesaplamada ülkelerin yıllık GSYH'si 365'e bölünerek günlük ekonomik üretim tahmin edildi. Ardından çalışanların yüzde 20'sinin iş bırakması ve bu kesimin günlük üretimin yaklaşık beşte birini gerçekleştirdiği varsayıldı. Bu yönteme göre İspanya'da bir günlük grevin ekonomik maliyetinin yaklaşık 930 milyon euro olması bekleniyor. Ülkenin 2025'teki 1,69 trilyon euroluk ekonomik üretimi, günlük ortalama 4,6 milyar euroya karşılık geliyor. Daha küçük ekonomilerde tahmini kayıp da azalıyor. Aynı büyüklükteki bir grevin Belçika ekonomisine yaklaşık 350 milyon euro, Portekiz ekonomisine ise 170 milyon euroya mal olabileceği hesaplanıyor. Grevlerin etkisi birkaç ay içinde telafi edilebiliyor Haberdeki hesaplamaların yaklaşık tahminler olduğu, grevlerin ekonomik etkisinin sektörlere göre farklılaştığı vurgulanıyor. Ulaşım, eğitim ve kamu hizmetlerinde faaliyetler daha fazla aksarken fabrikalar ve ofislerin önemli bir bölümü çalışmayı sürdürebiliyor. Fransa Merkez Bankası'nın 2023'teki emeklilik reformu karşıtı grevlere ilişkin hesaplaması, ekonomik kayıpların bir bölümünün sonraki aylarda telafi edilebildiğini gösteriyor. Banka, Mart ve Nisan 2023'teki grevlerin ilk çeyrekte ekonomik büyümeyi yaklaşık 0,1 puan düşürdüğünü, ikinci çeyrekte ise benzer büyüklükte bir toparlanma yaşandığını belirledi. Böylece kaybedilen ekonomik faaliyetin büyük bölümü üç ay içinde geri kazanıldı. Benzer şekilde Fransa Ulusal İstatistik ve Ekonomik Araştırmalar Enstitüsü (INSEE), 2018 baharındaki toplumsal eylemlerin GSYH'yi yaklaşık 0,1 puan azalttığını hesapladı. Ancak bazı kayıpların telafi edilmesi mümkün olmuyor. Greve katılan çalışanlar bir günlük ücretlerinden vazgeçerken, gerçekleşmeyen ekonomik faaliyetlerden vergi geliri elde edilemiyor. İptal edilen uçuşlar ve boş kalan otel odaları da sonradan telafi edilemeyen kayıplar arasında yer alıyor. Belçika'da grevlerin tekrarlanması dikkat çekiyor Avrupa Sendikalar Enstitüsü (ETUI) verileri, grevlerin sıklığının ekonomik etkiler açısından belirleyici olduğunu ortaya koyuyor. Belçika'da 2025 yılında grevler nedeniyle 1 milyon 354 bin 845 iş günü kaybedildi. Her 1000 çalışan başına 313 iş gününe karşılık gelen bu rakam, 1993'te kaydedilen 299 günlük önceki rekoru geride bıraktı. Hollanda'da geçen yıl 23 grev nedeniyle yaklaşık 60 bin iş günü kaybedildi. Almanya'da ise Ekonomik ve Sosyal Araştırmalar Enstitüsü (WSI), 2025'te grevlerden kaynaklanan kaybın yaklaşık 645 bin iş günü olduğunu hesapladı. Haberde, tek seferlik grevlerin ekonomik etkisinin sonraki dönemlerde telafi edilebildiği ancak sık tekrarlanan iş bırakma eylemlerinin üretim üzerinde daha kalıcı sonuçlar doğurabildiği değerlendiriliyor. İspanya'da grevin etkisi elektrik tüketiminden izlenecek İspanya'da 2012'deki genel grev sırasında katılımın ölçülmesinde elektrik tüketimi verilerinden yararlanılmıştı. İçişleri Bakanlığı, elektrik şebekesi işletmecisi Red Eléctrica'nın verilerine dayanarak sabahın erken saatlerinde elektrik talebinin normal seviyenin yüzde 11,4 altında kaldığını açıklamıştı. Mart 2012'deki grevde aynı saatte düşüş yüzde 15,4 olarak ölçülmüştü. Bu yılki grevde de elektrik tüketimi verilerinin katılıma ilişkin ilk göstergelerden biri olması bekleniyor. Sendikalar ve hükümetin açıklayacağı katılım rakamlarının ise birbirinden farklı olabileceği belirtiliyor. İspanya'daki grev, 29 Kasım'da yapılacak erken genel seçimden 18 gün önce düzenleniyor. Ülkede CCOO ve UGT sendikaları, çarşamba günü 24 saatlik genel grev çağrısında bulundu. Borsalar grevden etkilenmedi Grev çağrısına rağmen yatırımcıların İspanya piyasalarına yönelik belirgin bir tepki vermediği görülüyor. IBEX 35 endeksi pazartesi gününü 19 bin 742,5 puandan tamamladı. Endeks yıl başından bu yana yüzde 14,1 yükselirken tarihi zirvesinin yaklaşık yüzde 3 altında bulunuyor. Greve maruz kalabilecek şirketlerin hisselerinde de yıl genelinde yükseliş kaydedildi. İspanyol otel zinciri Meliá Hotels International'ın hisseleri yüzde 38, havalimanı işletmecisi Aena'nın hisseleri ise yüzde 21 değer kazandı. Euronews'ün değerlendirmesine göre, tek günlük grevlerin etkisi çoğunlukla geçici kalabilirken Belçika örneği, sık tekrarlanan iş bırakma eylemlerinin ekonomi üzerinde daha kalıcı bir yük oluşturabileceğine işaret ediyor.

İptal edilen uçuşlar ve boş kalan otel odaları da sonradan telafi edilemeyen kayıplar arasında yer alıyor. Belçika'da grevlerin tekrarlanması dikkat çekiyor Avrupa Sendikalar Enstitüsü (ETUI) verileri, grevlerin sıklığının ekonomik etkiler açısından belirleyici olduğunu ortaya koyuyor. Belçika'da 2025 yılında grevler nedeniyle 1 milyon 354 bin 845 iş günü kaybedildi. Her 1000 çalışan başına 313 iş gününe karşılık gelen bu rakam, 1993'te kaydedilen 299 günlük önceki rekoru geride bıraktı. Hollanda'da geçen yıl 23 grev nedeniyle yaklaşık 60 bin iş günü kaybedildi. Almanya'da ise Ekonomik ve Sosyal Araştırmalar Enstitüsü (WSI), 2025'te grevlerden kaynaklanan kaybın yaklaşık 645 bin iş günü olduğunu hesapladı. Haberde, tek seferlik grevlerin ekonomik etkisinin sonraki dönemlerde telafi edilebildiği ancak sık tekrarlanan iş bırakma eylemlerinin üretim üzerinde daha kalıcı sonuçlar doğurabildiği değerlendiriliyor. İspanya'da grevin etkisi elektrik tüketiminden izlenecek İspanya'da 2012'deki genel grev sırasında katılımın ölçülmesinde elektrik tüketimi verilerinden yararlanılmıştı. İçişleri Bakanlığı, elektrik şebekesi işletmecisi Red Eléctrica'nın verilerine dayanarak sabahın erken saatlerinde elektrik talebinin normal seviyenin yüzde 11,4 altında kaldığını açıklamıştı. Mart 2012'deki grevde aynı saatte düşüş yüzde 15,4 olarak ölçülmüştü. Bu yılki grevde de elektrik tüketimi verilerinin katılıma ilişkin ilk göstergelerden biri olması bekleniyor. Sendikalar ve hükümetin açıklayacağı katılım rakamlarının ise birbirinden farklı olabileceği belirtiliyor. İspanya'daki grev, 29 Kasım'da yapılacak erken genel seçimden 18 gün önce düzenleniyor. Ülkede CCOO ve UGT sendikaları, çarşamba günü 24 saatlik genel grev çağrısında bulundu. Borsalar grevden etkilenmedi Grev çağrısına rağmen yatırımcıların İspanya piyasalarına yönelik belirgin bir tepki vermediği görülüyor. IBEX 35 endeksi pazartesi gününü 19 bin 742,5 puandan tamamladı. Endeks yıl başından bu yana yüzde 14,1 yükselirken tarihi zirvesinin yaklaşık yüzde 3 altında bulunuyor. Greve maruz kalabilecek şirketlerin hisselerinde de yıl genelinde yükseliş kaydedildi. İspanyol otel zinciri Meliá Hotels International'ın hisseleri yüzde 38, havalimanı işletmecisi Aena'nın hisseleri ise yüzde 21 değer kazandı. Euronews'ün değerlendirmesine göre, tek günlük grevlerin etkisi çoğunlukla geçici kalabilirken Belçika örneği, sık tekrarlanan iş bırakma eylemlerinin ekonomi üzerinde daha kalıcı bir yük oluşturabileceğine işaret ediyor.
